mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 1200 units, indicating strengthening demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST and consumer confidence
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1200, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5%, indicating a tight labor market, wage pressures increase, leading to higher inflation expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 5%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising housing starts (HOUST) and increasing retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broadening demand, boosting S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, but only during non-recessionary periods.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in non-recession periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 6-month moving average signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 55% of instances when INDPRO < 6-month MA, or Rank IC < 0.015 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and increasing consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates tightening monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 240, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Always-on: the level of payroll employment (PAYEMS) is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as a strong labor market supports economic growth.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.015 over any 1.5-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly correlated with PAYEMS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The year-over-year change in GDP (GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 6%).
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when GDPC1 YoY > 3% and UNRATE < 6%, or Rank IC < 0.005 over any 1-year rolling window.
